newsitem.title: USA: Hein-Werner sees Q4, 1996 net up, sales off.
newsitem.headline: Hein-Werner sees Q4, 1996 net up, sales off.

text.p: Hein-Werner Corp said Wednesday it expects to report higher net income but lower sales for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year.

"Net income is expected to increase for the quarter and to more than double for 1996, reflecting ongoing improvement in Hein-Werner's core businesses, collision repair and fluid power, which are expected to drive future results," it said.

"Net sales for the quarter and 12 months of 1996 are expected to be down, reflecting weak business conditions in the U.S. engine rebuilding market and markets served by our French and German subsidiaries," the company said.
The company said operating profit for the quarter is expected to increase more than 10 percent from a year earlier, and year operating net is expected to increase more than 35 percent.
Audited figures will be available in late February.

Chief Executive Joseph Dindorf said, "Our U.S. collision repair business reported record earnings ... Hein-Werner now has strong distribution agreements in place in a number of Latin American countries as well as in mainland China and other Far Eastern countries. These are expected to produce important gains in 1997 and the years ahead."
Hein-Werner makes collision repair, engine rebuilding and fluid power equipment.
